title: Automata Forge
description: A from-scratch theory-of-computation lab spanning the WHOLE Chomsky hierarchy AND the temporal logic above it. NEWEST — v12 GAMES mode, the floor ABOVE model checking: INFINITE TWO-PLAYER GAMES ON FINITE GRAPHS, the computational engine of the modal MU-CALCULUS and of REACTIVE-CONTROLLER SYNTHESIS (parity games are polynomial-time inter-reducible with mu-calculus model checking, so this is the general machine the lab's LTL/CTL/CTL* checkers are special cases of). A token moves forever along a graph whose vertices are owned by two players; a winning condition decides the infinite play. All four canonical conditions are solved from scratch: REACHABILITY and SAFETY by a single ATTRACTOR least-fixpoint with positional strategy extraction, BUCHI (a liveness condition — an accepting state infinitely often) by the McNaughton/Zielonka peel-off fixpoint, and PARITY (highest priority seen infinitely often is even) by the full MCNAUGHTON-ZIELONKA recursion with two-player memoryless strategy synthesis. Every answer is PROVED by an independent, size-independent CERTIFICATE: pin each winner to its memoryless strategy and — since the opponent now controls all branching — 'can the opponent still win?' collapses to a graph question (a reachable cycle of the wrong parity, via restricted-subgraph Tarjan SCC), so if neither region admits a bad cycle and the two regions cover every vertex the partition is exactly right. Five interactive tabs: an ARENA you edit by clicking (recolour the target/hazard/accepting set, flip an owner, cycle a priority) or roll randomly; a SOLVE tab colouring the winning regions and drawing both positional strategies with a live certificate verdict; a PLAY tab where you take one side and the app answers with the optimal strategy, with loop detection and a per-condition verdict, plus a one-click 'watch both play optimally' lasso; a SYNTHESIS tab that reads Player 0's winning strategy back out as a CONTROLLER TABLE (state -> move) — a provably correct reactive program, the point of Church's synthesis problem; and a VERIFY tab that runs the whole proof harness in the browser. The differential harness proves the engine three independent ways sharing no logic: 1000 random arenas across all four conditions each yield a certificate-proven-exact solution; the fast solvers match a BRUTE-FORCE ORACLE (enumerate every memoryless strategy pair, simulate the deterministic play — the rules and nothing else) vertex-for-vertex on 180 small arenas; direct Buchi equals its parity encoding; parity role-duality (flip owners, shift priorities) swaps the winning regions exactly; and the certificate is shown to have TEETH by rejecting a deliberately corrupted solution; and TWO structurally-independent parity solvers — Zielonka's recursion and JURDZINSKI'S SMALL PROGRESS MEASURES (a least fixpoint over a lattice of tuples over the odd priorities) — are forced to agree on every arena, two famous algorithms sharing no code and one answer. NEWEST — v11 SYMBOLIC mode, a complete from-scratch SYMBOLIC MODEL CHECKER built on a hand-rolled REDUCED ORDERED BINARY DECISION DIAGRAM (ROBDD) engine — the data structure and technique behind SMV/NuSMV that pushed model checking from thousands of states to 10^20 and beyond. The BDD library is the real thing: a hash-consed unique table (canonical nodes, so equal functions share ONE id and equivalence is a pointer compare), the ITE-based Shannon-expansion recursion with a memoized computed table, restriction/cofactor, existential & universal quantification, variable renaming for current↔next bits, EXACT model counting (#SAT) and one-witness extraction. The system is encoded SYMBOLICALLY: a Kripke structure's states become bit-vectors over interleaved current/next variables, the transition relation and every Sat-set become BDDs, and the IDENTICAL Clarke-Emerson-Sistla CTL fixpoints run over BDDs — the pre-image pre∃(Y) as a RELATIONAL PRODUCT (∃ next. T ∧ Y[next]), EU/EF/AF/AU as LEAST and EG/AG/ER/AR as GREATEST fixpoints, convergence detected by a single canonical-id comparison. Three tabs make it tangible: a BDD EXPLORER that compiles any Boolean formula to its ROBDD, draws the decision DAG (hi/lo edges, shared nodes, reduced skips) with a live satisfying-path trace and a truth table, and lets you REORDER the variables to watch the node count swing from linear to exponential — the NP-hard ordering problem made visible; a TRANSITION-RELATION tab showing the symbolic encoding, the relation BDD (far smaller than the naive 2^2k table) and symbolic forward REACHABILITY as an animated μ-fixpoint; and a SYMBOLIC CHECK tab that runs the CTL fixpoints on BDDs, decodes each Sat-set back to state names and highlights it on the model graph, animates each fixpoint's per-round BDD node counts, and — the headline — DECODES the symbolic result and compares it LIVE against the explicit boolean-array checker for the exact model, proving the two engines agree state-for-state. The Verify tab differentially proves the whole engine (7/7) against code it shares NOTHING with: symbolic CTL agrees with the v9 EXPLICIT checker at EVERY state over 250 random (model, formula) pairs (0 mismatches), ITE matches brute-force truth tables, the algebra laws (double-negation, De Morgan, absorption, complement) hold by canonical id-equality, #SAT matches enumeration, the exists/forall identities and witness soundness hold, the propositional parser round-trips, and symbolic reachability equals explicit BFS over 200 models. ALSO — v10 CTL* mode, a complete from-scratch CTL* MODEL CHECKER that closes the temporal-logic hierarchy: CTL* is the logic ABOVE both LTL and CTL, dropping CTL's rule that a path quantifier must hug one temporal operator so E (some path) / A (all paths) bind an ARBITRARY path formula — letting the temporal operators nest freely. E[G F p] ('some path is fair') and A[(G F req) -> (G F ack)] (strong-fairness response) are expressible in NEITHER CTL nor LTL alone; CTL* is exactly the closure that contains them, alongside the linear idiom F G p and the branching idiom A G E F reset. It is checked by the EMERSON-LEI algorithm, which is the genuine SYNTHESIS of the lab's two temporal engines: strip the INNERMOST quantifier, decide E rho ('some path from here satisfies the LTL body rho') by the v8 GPVW/Vardi-Wolper Büchi-automaton emptiness check run per state — and A rho = ¬E¬rho by its dual — name the result with a fresh proposition, substitute upward, and finish on a Boolean residual. So the OUTSIDE is the v9 branching labelling and the INSIDE is the v8 LTL automata, glued by atom introduction. The Decompose tab animates the elimination round by round — each fresh label lighting up its Sat-set on the model graph, with a REPLAYABLE witnessing/refuting lasso per start state — and a Formula tab classifies any formula as linear / CTL / proper CTL*. The live Verify tab differentially proves the whole chain (7/7) against engines that share NO code with the checker: on the CTL fragment the Emerson-Lei checker agrees with the v9 SYMBOLIC-FIXPOINT labelling engine at every state over 700 random (model, formula) pairs (0 mismatches); on full CTL* the production GPVW emptiness agrees with an INDEPENDENT Tarjan-SCC path-existence oracle over 350 pairs (0 mismatches); on the linear fragment A rho / E rho agree with the v8 DIRECT ω-word semantics over 400 pairs; plus the A rho = ¬E¬rho duality, certificate soundness (every witness lasso is a real path replayed under the direct semantics), and every gallery verdict. ALSO — v9 BRANCHING mode, a complete from-scratch CTL MODEL CHECKER that completes the temporal-logic story: where the Logic mode is LINEAR time (one path at a time), Computation Tree Logic reasons about the TREE of futures, pairing every temporal operator with a path quantifier E (some path) or A (all paths) — EX/AX, EF/AF, EG/AG and the bracketed E[a U b]/A[a R b]. It is checked by a completely different algorithm: the LABELLING ALGORITHM of Clarke-Emerson-Sistla, computing Sat(psi) — the set of states where each subformula holds — bottom-up, with the temporal operators as LEAST fixpoints (EU/AU/EF/AF) and GREATEST fixpoints (EG/AG/ER/AR) of a pre-image step, and the Labelling tab ANIMATES the whole approximant chain Z0, Z1, … converging to the fixpoint. It witnesses verdicts with replayable CERTIFICATES — a finite path to a bad state, or a goal-avoiding LASSO — every per-state obligation independently verified, a failing formula certified by the witness of its negation in NNF. The headline properties (AG EF restart — 'from every reachable state the system can be reset', AG EF up — recoverability) are provably INEXPRESSIBLE in LTL, the whole reason branching time earns its own mode; the About tab makes the CTL/LTL incomparability concrete. The live Verify tab differentially proves the chain (7/7): the symbolic fixpoint checker agrees at EVERY state with a SECOND, structurally-independent oracle that decides the operators by explicit backward-BFS reachability and Tarjan SCC analysis — 0 mismatches over 400 random (model, formula) pairs — plus adequacy of the {not, and, EX, EU, EG} rewrite, the textbook fixpoint identities, certificate soundness, and ACTL matching the LTL semantics on linear models. ALSO — v8 LOGIC mode, a complete from-scratch LTL MODEL CHECKER that lifts the lab from finite words to the INFINITE traces of reactive systems. Write a Linear Temporal Logic formula and watch the GPVW TABLEAU (Gerth-Peled-Vardi-Wolper 1995 — the construction inside SPIN's ltl2ba) turn it into a generalized BÜCHI AUTOMATON by unrolling a U b ≡ b ∨ (a ∧ X(aUb)) and a R b ≡ b ∧ (a ∨ X(aRb)), then DEGENERALIZE it (the Baier-Katoen counter construction) to an ordinary Büchi automaton — the ω-word cousin of the NFA — drawn with the app's pan/zoom/export renderer (propositional guards under each state, double-ring accepts, a start arrow per initial state). Build a system as a KRIPKE STRUCTURE in a tiny DSL, then MODEL-CHECK it by the VARDI-WOLPER automata-theoretic method: form the product A(¬φ) ⊗ M, search for a reachable accepting state on a cycle, and get back either a proof the property holds or an ANIMATED LASSO COUNTEREXAMPLE (a stem leading into a forever-repeated loop, with a playhead). An ω-word tracer checks any ultimately-periodic word against both the automaton and an INDEPENDENT direct-semantics oracle, and the live Verify tab differentially proves the whole chain — across 400 random (formula, word) pairs the automaton for φ accepts a word IFF the independent LTL semantics says it satisfies φ (0 mismatches), exactly one of A(φ)/A(¬φ) accepts each word, and every counterexample is replayed as a genuine violating model path. ALSO — v7 Learn mode, a complete from-scratch implementation of ANGLUIN'S L* ACTIVE-LEARNING algorithm: the target machine is HIDDEN and the app must RECONSTRUCT its minimal DFA by asking only membership and equivalence queries — and the teacher is the lab's OWN product-automaton equivalence check, which hands back the shortest distinguishing counterexample. Watch the iconic OBSERVATION TABLE fill in cell by cell (rows coloured by signature, so same colour = same discovered state; closedness defects flagged in the boundary the instant before they are promoted), scrub through every atomic step — each membership bit, each closing and consistency repair, each conjecture and counterexample — toggle between the Angluin-1987 (add every prefix to S) and Rivest-Schapire-1993 (binary-search one distinguishing suffix into E) counterexample rules and see RS use far fewer queries, and watch the hypothesis DFA grow until it provably equals the target, with a live read-out of membership/equivalence query counts. It converges to exactly the Hopcroft-minimal DFA — differential-tested over 16 curated + 400 random targets under both strategies. ALSO — v6 Parse mode, a complete from-scratch PARSER GENERATOR built on the FIRST/FOLLOW engine: the top-down LL(1) predictive table M[A,a] (with conflict detection for left-recursion / common-prefix grammars) and the ENTIRE bottom-up tower LR(0) < SLR(1) < LALR(1) < LR(1) — the canonical item-set automaton (closure/goto, LR(1) lookahead propagation via FIRST(βa), and LALR by core-merging proven to yield exactly |LR(0)| states), drawn with the app's pan/zoom/export renderer; the ACTION/GOTO parse tables with shift-reduce & reduce-reduce conflicts flagged; a live grammar CLASSIFIER (which classes the grammar belongs to, and why the rest fail); and ANIMATED stack-driven parsers — a predictive LL(1) parser building the leftmost tree and a shift-reduce LR parser building the rightmost tree in reverse, both step-scrubbable. A curated gallery puts each grammar on a different rung (Knuth's pointer grammar is LALR(1)-not-SLR(1); the classic reduce/reduce-on-merge grammar is LR(1)-not-LALR(1); dangling-else is an unavoidable shift/reduce). Every parser is differential-tested to accept exactly L(G) against the Earley oracle. REGULAR (level 3): compile a regex into a parse tree, Thompson e-NFA, subset-construction DFA, Hopcroft-minimized DFA and a Brzozowski-derivative DFA; step strings through any of them; compare two regexes via the product automaton (union, intersection, difference, symmetric difference), decide equivalence/containment and prove inequality with the shortest distinguishing string; or draw your own automaton in Build mode, with a Myhill-Nerode table and direct NFA-to-regex. CONTEXT-FREE (level 2) — Grammar mode: analyze a grammar (nullable / generating / reachable / useless, FIRST & FOLLOW), normalize to Chomsky Normal Form step-by-step, recognize strings two ways (CYK table + Earley chart), render the derivation tree with ambiguity detection, sample the language, compile to a pushdown automaton with an animated stack, and play the CFL pumping lemma. NEW in v5 — Machine mode, the TOP of the hierarchy (level 0/1): a single-tape Turing machine simulator with an animated two-way tape, full configuration trace, a state-transition diagram and a delta-table, a linear-bounded (context-sensitive) mode, and a gallery of deciders for languages no grammar can describe — a-n b-n c-n and w#w are NOT context-free yet a TM decides them live — plus transducers, Rado's busy beaver, and a nondeterministic-TM configuration search. Bridges run both ways: every regex becomes a right-linear grammar AND a read-only Turing machine. No libraries — every parser, automaton algorithm, the graph layout and the SVG renderer are hand-written and differential-tested.
